capitals.note: The county took its name from the hill in Untertürkheim 'on which Wattenberg Castle stood until 1819'; the page gives no capital before Stuttgart, so this seat is an inference (confidence 1).

capitals.name: Stuttgart
capitals.note: Infobox capital Stuttgart; the page says Stuttgart 'was included within the county' in 1251. During the 1442-1482 partition the Urach line (Ludwig) ruled from Bad Urach with Tübingen.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row; its lands lie in 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States'. The county page dates Konrad I to 1081 and gives no extent; the 18 km radius is a stand-in (soft).

correction.text: the county after Stuttgart came in 1251 and the Württembergs 'expand[ed] into the duchy' of Swabia after 1250; Tübingen and Urach already counted (they pass to the Urach line in 1442)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the county page gives no area; the 40 km radius around Stuttgart reaches Tübingen and Urach. Soft.

Montbéliard (a 20 km radius, about 1,250 km2) is a detached possession, held from 1444 by Ludwig of Urach and 'adjudicated' to him on Henriette's death.

Montbéliard was separated for a younger son in 1617 and 'fell back to Württemberg in 1723' (Montbéliard page); it stays in the shape because the line was Württemberg's. The Thirty Years' War occupation after Nördlingen (1634) is an occupation event, not a redraw.

ledger.note: 1081: Konrad I of Württemberg is first recorded; the Wirtemberg castle gives the county its name. 'The first family member mentioned in records was Konrad I, in 1081, who is believed to have built the castle'; infobox 'County founded by Conrad I: before 1081 1083' (the page's own double year).

region.text: the lands round the Wirtemberg castle at Untertürkheim, near Stuttgart

ledger.note: 1250: the Hohenstaufen reign over the Duchy of Swabia ends and 'let the Württembergs expand into the duchy'. The page names no town but Stuttgart (1251) and gives no extent, so the county grows to the 40 km radius shape by 1251 at confidence 2.

region.text: Swabian lands round Stuttgart, Tübingen and Urach that the county absorbed after the Hohenstaufen

ledger.note: 1251: Stuttgart comes to the county. 'Stuttgart was included within the county as a result of the marriage between Ulrich I and Mechthild of Baden in 1251.' The page does not name the former owner; Baden is the bride's house.

1442: the Treaty of Nürtingen divides the county. 'Ulrich received the Stuttgart area (Württemberg-Stuttgart)' and 'Ludwig received the Bad Urach section (Württemberg-Urach)', including Tübingen; the Duchy page: 'had split in half along the two branches of the family in 1442 by the Treaty of Nürtingen'. Both lines are the House of Württemberg and neither has a dossier, so no land changes owner: recorded as a rename (caption only); a split with no counterpart would send the county to nobody for 1442-1443. The 1251 and 1444 keyframes draw the land.

1444: Montbéliard passes to the Urach line. 'Urach gained Montbéliard after the death of Henriette in 1444'; the Montbéliard page: 'From 1444 onwards it was held by the House of Württemberg', and dates the Eberhard-Henriette marriage to 1407 where the county page has a 1397 betrothal.

region.text: the county of Montbéliard (Mömpelgard) in the west, beyond the Vosges

ledger.note: 1482: Eberhard V reunites the county. 'As a result of the Treaty of Münsingen in 1482' the Stuttgart and Urach lines are joined again; the Duchy page: 'In 1482, he united the two parts of the future duchy.' Both lines are the House of Württemberg and Urach has no dossier, so no land changes owner: recorded as a rename (caption only). The page: 'As a result of the Treaty of Münsingen in 1482 and the Treaty of Esslingen in 1492, Count Eberhard V succeeded in reuniting Württemberg'.
21 July 1495: the county becomes a duchy. 'The Duchy of Württemberg was formed when, at the Diet of Worms, 21 July 1495'; the first duke is Eberhard (I/V) 1495-1496.

6 February 1520: the Swabian League sells the duchy to Charles V. Ulrich was expelled (February 1512 first, then driven out in 1519 after he 'stormed the Imperial City of Reutlingen' eight days after Maximilian I's death on 12 January 1519); 'the League sold the duchy to the new Holy Roman Emperor, Charles V, on 6 February 1520, for 220,000 florins', who turned it over to Archduke Ferdinand on 31 March 1522.

region.text: the Duchy of Württemberg, held by the Swabian League and then by Charles V and Ferdinand I (1520-1534)

ledger.note: June 1534: Ulrich returns. On 13 May 'the troops of the Habsburgs were completely defeated at the Battle of Lauffen' and 'in June 1534 a treaty was negotiated at Kaaden' by which Ulrich 'was recognized as duke by Ferdinand, but was to hold Württemberg under Austrian suzerainty'. The page does not say when the suzerainty ended, so no vassal event is drawn.

region.text: the Duchy of Württemberg, restored to Ulrich

ledger.note: September 1634: the Imperial army takes Württemberg. After Nördlingen (5-6 September 1634) 'The Imperial army retook most of Württemberg and moved into the Rhineland'; the page gives no date for the occupation itself.

region.text: most of Württemberg, retaken by the Imperial army after Nördlingen

ledger.note: 1648: the Imperial occupation of Württemberg ends with the Peace of Westphalia. The Nördlingen page does not date the withdrawal (page silent); the Duchy page has no Thirty Years' War territory. A gap-filler should open 'Eberhard III, Duke of Württemberg'.

November 1793: the French Republic occupies Montbéliard. 'In 1793, the County of Montbéliard was occupied by the First French Republic' (more precisely November 1793); Duke Frederick II Eugene 'finally renounce[d] all rights to Montbéliard' in 1796.

region.text: the County of Montbéliard, annexed to Haute-Saône and later Mont-Terrible

ledger.note: February 1803: the duchy becomes an electorate. 'In 1803, Napoleon raised the duchy to be the Electorate of Württemberg' (infobox 'Raised to Electorate: 1803'); the Final Recess of February 1803 gave Württemberg about 1,500 km2 and 120,000 people against 400 km2 and 30,000 lost (mediatisation page); the king's title follows on 1 January 1806.

region.text: the duchy, continued as the Electorate of Württemberg

wars.outcome: Ulrich is expelled; the duchy passes to the Habsburgs (Charles V 1520, Ferdinand 1522).
wars.note: No Wikipedia article for this war was opened; named from the Duchy and Ulrich pages.

wars.name: Ulrich's reconquest of Württemberg

zones.text: the Duchy of Württemberg: Lauffen 13 May 1534

wars.outcome: Habsburg defeat at Lauffen; the Treaty of Kaaden (June 1534) recognises Ulrich as duke under Austrian suzerainty.

wars.name: Battle of Nördlingen and the Imperial reoccupation

zones.text: Württemberg, retaken by the Imperial army after 5-6 September 1634

wars.outcome: The Protestant defeat at Nördlingen lets the Imperial army retake most of Württemberg; the Peace of Prague (May 1635) dissolves the Heilbronn League.
wars.note: Thirty Years' War; end year 1648 is the Peace of Westphalia (page silent on Württemberg).

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession (Villars's invasion)
wars.outcome: A French invasion under Villars in 1707; the Duchy page records no territorial change.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundary lines; the duchy was a patchwork of enclaves and Habsburg, Baden and imperial-city neighbours. The only size figure is 'over 8,000 square kilometres' for the duchy.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (7 pages opened). New state: Cliopatria has no pre-1803 Württemberg row (its lands are in 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States'); the 1803..1805 Electorate of Württemberg row belongs to eu-20.

ONE STATE, TWO NAMES. The county (1081-1495) and the duchy (1495-1803) are one state with a rename event (rule 2). The dossier ends in February 1803 where Cliopatria's electorate starts.

SHAPES ARE RADIUS READINGS. No page gives the county's or the duchy's boundary. The 52 km circle round Stuttgart (8,850 km2) is checked against the Duchy page's 'over 8,000 square kilometres' (ratio 1.1); the 40 km and 18 km circles for the county are guesses at soft edges. Montbéliard is a 20 km circle at 6.80E 47.51N. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Montbéliard' (place), 'Tübingen' (place), 'Bad Urach' (place), 'Wirtemberg' (castle).

NOT SETTLED. (1) 1397 (betrothal, County page) against 1407 (marriage, Montbéliard page): the 1444 passage is the only dated step used. (2) Montbéliard was a cadet appanage from 1617 to 1723; drawn as Württemberg throughout. (3) Austrian suzerainty over Württemberg from the Treaty of Kaaden (June 1534): the pages opened do not say when it ended, so no vassal_start/vassal_end is recorded; the Treaty of Kaaden page did not load (WebFetch url_not_found for https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Kaaden), so the terms come from the Ulrich page and a gap-filler should find the right title. (4) The Imperial occupation of 1634-1648 is dated only at its start; the end is confidence 1. (5) Other acquisitions (Böblingen, Urach, Tübingen, Heidenheim, the Black Forest) were not on the pages. (6) Rulers: the Duchy page gives only Eberhard I (1495-1496) and Frederick III (1797-1803) and calls the first duke Eberhard I in the infobox, Eberhard V in the text; a list of dukes of Württemberg was not opened, so none is given. (7) The Peace of Westphalia and the Peace of Prague (May 1635) change no Württemberg land on the pages opened.

COUNTERPARTS FOR OTHER GROUPS: county-of-montbeliard (Montbéliard, a Württemberg possession 1444-1793), margraviate-of-baden (the 1251 Stuttgart marriage and the neighbour to the west), swabian-league (the 1519-1520 buyer), electorate-of-wurttemberg (eu-20).
